# Section D results: can the photo alone warn that a heart-rate reading is wrong? (C3)

*Generated by `scripts/analysis/section_D.py`. Rules fixed before the results were seen (see the script header).*

## C3 verdict: **INCONCLUSIVE (the new 100 hold 86 wrong readings; the rule needs at least 100)**

- Trained on 1509 images of the first 50 (89 wrong readings); scored once on 1265 images of the new 100 (86 wrong readings; images where the digitiser gave no reading are left out of the primary target).
- AUC = **0.858** (95% recording-level interval 0.81 to 0.91). Oracle told the exact damage type and level: **0.827** (0.77 to 0.90).
- Best single score, chosen on the first 50 only: **blur_log** (lower=worse), AUC on the new 100 = 0.814.
- The word 'usable' is not used. The verdict is worded 'within these six damage types' because the scores were designed around the same six damage types.

## Exploratory: inside one damage type and level (can the scores tell WHICH pages are wrong?)

| damage | images | wrong_readings | auc_within_damage |
|---|---|---|---|
| resolution level 5 | 99 | 47 | 0.521 |
| blur level 5 | 98 | 17 | 0.476 |

An AUC near 0.5 here means the detector recognises how damaged a page is, not which damaged pages will fail.
